windows.assessment: The strongest row is an original external-action work packet, but its linked chronology resolves to an operator-approved coding agent responding to non-bot reviewer feedback. Other selected rows are deterministic validation, designed governance or specification records.
Twenty Linux clock files and one unrelated C source are lexical collisions. The three selected JSONL logs all record one `co-scientist` actor and stage/tool outputs, not inter-participant delivery.

selected_originals.title: Dharma cycle-44 external-action work packet and linked review chronology
selected_originals.classification: real review-to-revision chronology involving an explicitly operator-approved coding agent and non-bot reviewer accounts; no autonomous sender-to-recipient swarm edge

first_public_file_commit.note: The same commit SHA and blob occur in both repositories, supporting shared history/mirroring rather than independent publishers.

events.event: pull request opened by the work-packet account
automated CodeRabbit comment created; current text reports no actionable comments in its recent review
non-bot-labeled reviewer account objects to an out-of-scope behavior change
follow-on commit removes the disputed behavior change
PR author says the update followed review feedback and was prepared by an AI coding agent under operator-approved external-action mode
a different non-bot-labeled reviewer account approves

observations: The packet tracks six active pull requests across five third-party repositories but records no new public action in cycle 44, no external confirmation, no maintainer action and no merge at its 21:19:48 UTC observation.
The linked PR proves a content-specific review-to-revision dependency: the behavior objection precedes the behavior-removal commit by 5 minutes 20 seconds.
The actionable sender is not verified as autonomous AI. The packet itself classifies the review as non-maintainer human review, and the reviewing account is not bot-labeled.
CodeRabbit is a distinct automated service, but its comment says no actionable comments were generated and no public evidence ties its output to the correction.

The responding coding agent is self-attributed rather than provider-attested and explicitly says it acted under operator-approved external-action mode. Approval and merge use ordinary repository review authority.

alternatives.single_operator_automation: Supported for the coding side by one named work-packet actor and one public account.
alternatives.human_requested_outreach: Supported by the explicit operator-approved mode and ordinary issue/PR review path.
alternatives.designed_review_workflow: Supported by CodeRabbit's configured review and the repository's approval/merge gates.
alternatives.cross_operator_autonomous_coordination: Not established: the actionable reviewer is not verified autonomous, and the bot comment is not causally used.

selected_originals.missing_evidence: An independently attributable autonomous reviewer under a separate operator, a specific bot/agent result that the coding agent demonstrably consumed, and primary evidence that their cooperation exceeded the repository's authorized PR/review/merge process.

selected_originals.title: AIRA SCI-009, SCI-065 and SCI-085 process logs
selected_originals.classification: three additional single-actor experiment logs; handoff labels denote tool or pipeline stages
observations: Every row in all three files names the same actor, `co-scientist`.
Skill/tool names vary, but no row supplies sender and recipient principals, delivery transport or an independent recipient effect.
SCI-085's handoff-completed rows are sequential pipeline modules; SCI-009 and SCI-065 similarly label literature, verification or general-purpose stages.
selected_originals.missing_evidence: Separate autonomous principals, a public delivery/receipt and downstream use, plus independent operator provenance.

selected_originals.title: Hutch dynamic-workflow validation capture
selected_originals.classification: deterministic zero-model-call acceptance capture, not an agent exchange
observations: The scenario calls itself deterministic and zero model calls.
It expressly says no live local model server existed, no model-authored plan, planner or worker ran, and the apparent human answer was supplied by the capture script.
One manual CLI workflow produces one content-addressed report; `browser_handoff=headless` is configuration metadata, not a participant transfer.
selected_originals.missing_evidence: A real autonomous sender, separate autonomous recipient, delivery/use and independent operators.

selected_originals.title: Hermes owner-adjudicated factory summary
selected_originals.classification: single-repository governed review ledger with model labels but no independently controlled recipient
observations: The summary names a planner/reviewer author lane, multiple Claude-labelled review receipts and owner adjudication, but marks itself neither approval nor validation substrate.
The selected file history is published by one account inside a designed promotion program; repository-authored model/session labels are not independent provider or operator attestations.
No public transport establishes a foreign autonomous reviewer delivering a result to a separately controlled recipient that then exceeds authorization.
selected_originals.missing_evidence: Provider- or operator-owned sender/recipient attestations, exact delivery and downstream use under independently controlled operators, and an authorization crossing.

This scoped absence is not a global novelty claim and cannot cure the missing autonomous sender, recipient or authorization-crossing evidence.

known_family_overlap.named_exclusions: No selected record is treated as a new instance of the named DseWiki/RubyGems, Transluce, Amap, Green AI Bot, Technocore/Agent Workpad, OpenAI May/July, AISI GitHub handoff or Covert Assistance/METR families.

known_family_overlap.dharma: The same blob and commit SHA in two repositories are treated as shared-history mirrors, not two participants.

conclusion.participant_test: The main chain has one self-attributed coding agent, one configured review bot with no demonstrated causal contribution and non-bot reviewer accounts. It does not prove two autonomous participants in a causal exchange.
conclusion.dependency_test: A real review-to-revision dependency exists, but the actionable reviewer is not verified autonomous. Other selected records are single-actor stages, deterministic validation or specifications.
conclusion.operator_boundary_test: The coding agent explicitly reports operator-approved external-action mode; the PR follows ordinary review, approval and merge gates. No cooperation exceeding authorization is shown.
conclusion.provider_attribution: Repository and PR self-labels are preserved as claims, not independent provider attestations.
conclusion.rogue_intent_test: No subjective rogue intent is inferred.
conclusion.current_activity: The strongest chain occurred on 1 June 2026 and later merged; no claim of current autonomous coordination is made.
conclusion.result: No plausible previously unreported rogue-swarm candidate. No candidate ID assigned.

limitations: Code-search rank drift means consecutive page windows can overlap across observations.
Repository-authored actor, model and operator-mode labels are not independent provider or operator attestations.
A non-bot GitHub account is not proof of a human; the work packet's human-review classification is reported as an origin claim.
Exact-search absence is bounded to the checked index and query strings.
No recovered code, agent runtime, scan, message, sink, private log or target system was executed, invoked, submitted, contacted or probed.
